name: Innr SP 242 (UK)

radios.note: Zigbee on 2.4 GHz (max 10 dBm per the manual). Acts as a Zigbee repeater.

matter.note: Zigbee-only plug; Innr doesn't mention Matter for it and no CSA listing was found.

apple_home.note: Innr's Works-with page says Innr devices on a Hue Bridge are not passed to Apple HomeKit. No source covers other routes, so not marked 'no'.

google_home.note: Innr's Works-with page doesn't list Google Home for this plug.

alexa.via: Echo with Zigbee hub, Hue Bridge or SmartThings
alexa.note: Pairs directly with Echo models that have a built-in Zigbee hub (e.g. Echo 4th gen, Studio, Show 10), or via a Hue Bridge or SmartThings.

smartthings.note: Innr lists SmartThings as a supported Zigbee hub.

home_assistant.note: Innr says its products work with ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT, including plug power metering, but it doesn't support those setups itself. Zigbee2MQTT lists the SP 242.

hubRequired.note: Zigbee plug: needs a Zigbee hub such as a Hue Bridge, SmartThings, an Echo with Zigbee, Homey or the Innr bridge.

localControl.note: No Innr statement on control without internet found.

energyMonitoring.note: Reports power, voltage, current and energy. Innr says Philips Hue doesn't show the readings; SmartThings, Hubitat, Homey and Home Assistant do.

maxLoadWatts.note: Innr's manual gives a 13 A total current limit; no watt figure found.

summary: The Innr SP 242 is a UK (Type G) Zigbee smart plug with power metering. It needs a Zigbee hub: Innr lists Hue, SmartThings, Echo speakers with a built-in Zigbee hub, and Home Assistant via ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT. Its manual gives a 13 A limit.
caveats: Needs a Zigbee hub; there is no Wi-Fi.
Philips Hue can switch it but doesn't show its energy readings.

sources.title: Innr Smart Plug with Power Monitoring, works with Hue* and Zigbee Hubs
